models.job: The one that lives in the boot.
models.intro: Minu V3 is UPPAbaby's compact stroller. It folds one-handed to about the size of a carry-on, stands on its own, and is ready from birth as sold with the included infant insert. It is the pram for families who move a lot, live with stairs or a small boot, and want one stroller that covers the newborn stage and the toddler years without being a full-size pram.
models.facts: Minu V3 (stroller); 7.6 kg; folds to 25 x 45 x 55 cm; up to 1; works from birth; basket 9.1 kg

models.job: Not a full size pram. More than a travel pram.
models.intro: Kona is the mid-size pram in the UPPAbaby range. It has a reversible, from-birth seat and a full-size basket, but a slim footprint that clears a shop aisle and turns a tight corner. It suits parents who do not want the bulk of a full-size pram but need more than a travel stroller can carry.
models.facts: Kona (pram); 9.9 kg; folds to 34.0 x 53.3 x 65.5 cm; up to 1; works from birth; basket 13.6 kg

models.job: The everyday single, without the bulk.
models.intro: Cruz V3 is the full-size single pram. It has the same seat quality, canopy and basket as Vista in a narrower, lighter frame, and it is suitable from birth with the included infant insert. Cruz is for one child at a time: it does not take a second seat. Choose it over Vista when you are confident one child is the plan, or when boot space matters more than the option to add a sibling later.
models.facts: Cruz V3 (pram); up to 1; works from birth; basket 13.6 kg

models.job: Two children, side by side, through a standard doorway.
models.intro: Minu Duo is a side-by-side double stroller narrow enough to pass through a standard 73 cm doorway. Both seats are the same size, both recline, and both are usable from birth, which is unusual in a double this compact. It is the answer for twins, or for two children close in age, when a tandem is too long and a full double is too wide.
models.facts: Minu Duo (stroller); folds to 33 x 70.6 x 60.2 cm; up to 2; works from birth; basket 11.3 kg

models.job: For the trails and the long runs.
models.intro: Ridge V2 is the all-terrain jogger. Never-flat tyres, a locking front wheel and a long wheelbase make it stable at running pace and on gravel, sand and grass. It is the largest pram in the range folded, so it suits families with boot space who want one pram that handles a run and a beach track as easily as a footpath.
models.facts: Ridge V2 (pram); 13.7 kg; folds to 49.5 x 65 x 91.4 cm; up to 2; works from birth; basket 9.0 kg

models.job: One pram, up to three children.
models.intro: Vista V3 is the full-size pram built to grow with a family rather than a child. It ships with the bassinet included, so it is ready from birth out of the box, and it converts to carry two children with a RumbleSeat or a second bassinet, or three with a PiggyBack board. More than thirty configurations come off the one frame. It is the most expensive pram in the range and the only one that can absorb a second and third child without being replaced.
models.facts: Vista V3 (pram); up to 3; works from birth; basket 13.6 kg

capsule.name: Mesa
capsule.intro: Mesa is the UPPAbaby infant car capsule. It clicks straight onto a Vista, Cruz or Kona frame with no adapters, and onto Minu, Minu Duo and Ridge with the matching adapter set. That means a sleeping baby moves from car to pram without being unbuckled.

faq.q: Can I use the Vista V3 from birth?
faq.a: Yes, straight out of the box. The bassinet is included, not an accessory you add later, so a newborn can lie flat on day one. The toddler seat takes over at around six months.

faq.q: How many children can a Vista V3 carry?
faq.a: Up to three on the one frame. Two seated, using a RumbleSeat or a second bassinet, and a third standing on a PiggyBack board that clips to the rear axle.

faq.q: Will a Vista V3 fit in my boot?
faq.a: Folded with the toddler seat attached it is 41.4 x 65.3 x 85.9 cm. With the seat removed it drops to 28.7 x 65.3 x 82.9 cm. Measure the shortest side of your boot opening, not the space inside it. The opening is what stops a pram going in.

faq.q: How heavy is the Vista V3?
faq.a: 12.5 kg with the frame and toddler seat together. The frame alone is 9 kg, the seat 3.5 kg and the bassinet 4.2 kg, so it can be lifted in parts.

faq.q: Does the Mesa capsule fit the Vista V3?
faq.a: Yes, directly. The Mesa clicks onto the frame with no adapters, so a sleeping baby goes from the car to the pram without being unbuckled. Maxi-Cosi, Nuna, Joie and BeSafe capsules fit with the Vista upper car seat adapter.

faq.q: What is included in the box?
faq.a: Pram frame, toddler seat, bassinet, bumper bar, seasonal seat liner, toddler seat bug shield, toddler seat rain shield, bassinet bug shield, storage bag and the three year warranty. Nothing on that list is sold separately.

faq.q: How much can the basket hold?
faq.a: 13.6 kg, which is the largest in the range. It is reachable from either side, including when the seat faces you.

faq.q: Does the seat face me or face out?
faq.a: Both. The toddler seat is reversible, so it can face you while they are small and face forward when they would rather watch the world.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Vista V3 and the Cruz V3?
faq.a: The Vista takes a second and a third child; the Cruz carries one and no accessory changes that. The Vista also includes the bassinet, where the Cruz needs one bought separately. The Cruz is narrower, lighter and less expensive.

faq.q: How wide is the Vista V3 when it is open?
faq.a: 65.3 cm across, which is the figure that matters for shop aisles and front doors. Opened out it is 92.7 x 65.3 x 100.3 cm.

faq.q: How long is the warranty in Australia?
faq.a: Three years from purchase against manufacturing defects, plus complimentary maintenance checks for up to ten years under Lifetime Service Support. Register your pram to activate it.

faq.q: Is buying direct cheaper than a retailer?

faq.q: Can I try one before I buy?

faq.a: 7.6 kg, the lightest pram we sell. In its box it is 9.4 kg, which matters if you are checking it as luggage.

faq.a: Yes, and it stands on its own once folded, so it does not need a wall to lean against on a train platform or in a hotel room.

faq.q: Can the Minu V3 carry two children?

faq.q: Is the Minu V3 seat reversible?
faq.a: No, the seat faces forward only. That is part of how the fold gets this small. If you want a parent-facing seat, look at the Cruz V3 or the Vista V3.

faq.q: How wide is the Minu V3?
faq.a: 45 cm across, opened out to 88 x 45 x 104 cm. It is the narrowest pram in the range.

faq.q: Is the Minu V3 suitable as an only pram?
faq.a: For a lot of families, yes. It is from birth, it takes a capsule with the adapter, and it goes to 22 kg. It is worth thinking twice if you walk long distances daily on rough ground, where a larger wheel earns its keep.

Babies outgrow a capsule by height before weight. Move to the next seat when the top of the head is level with the top of the shell, or at the weight limit, whichever comes first. Do not wait for the first birthday if the head is already there, and do not turn a baby forward facing early because they seem to want the view. faq.q: Is the Mesa approved for use in Australia?
faq.a: Yes. Every child restraint sold in Australia must meet AS/NZS 1754, the Australian and New Zealand standard, and the Mesa sold here is the Australian version, approved as a Type A2 rearward-facing infant restraint. It is not the US or European Mesa; those are not legal to use in Australia.

faq.q: How long can my baby stay in the Mesa?
faq.a: From Birth (2.0 kg) to 15 kg, which is approximately birth to 12 months. Move up when your baby reaches the weight limit, or when the top of their head is level with the top of the shell, whichever comes first. Height matters more than birthdays.

faq.q: Does my baby have to face backwards?
faq.a: Under the Australian road rules a child under six months must travel in an approved rearward-facing restraint, and from six months to four years may stay rearward facing or move to a forward-facing seat with an inbuilt harness. Rearward facing protects the head and neck best, so the advice from every Australian safety body is to keep a baby rearward facing for as long as the seat allows, not to turn them at six months. The Mesa is rearward facing only.

faq.q: ISOFIX or the seatbelt, which is safer?
faq.a: Neither is safer when fitted correctly; both are tested to the same standard. ISOFIX is quicker and harder to get wrong, and the base shows green indicators when both connectors are locked. The seatbelt install works in any car and relies on the built-in lock-off, which is the step people skip. Whichever you use, the load leg must sit firmly on the floor.

faq.q: Can I use the Mesa without the base?
faq.a: The Australian Mesa is designed to be used with its base, which is what carries the ISOFIX connectors and the load leg. Check the Australian manual for the approved installation methods before you fit it any other way.

faq.q: Can the Mesa go on a plane?
faq.a: Yes. CASA approved for aircraft use, so it can be used in an aircraft seat on airlines that permit child restraints. Check with the airline when you book, and register the capsule under TravelSafe before you fly.

faq.q: My car was in an accident. Is the capsule still safe?
faq.a: Treat it as not safe. A restraint that was in a vehicle during a collision may have damage you cannot see. UPPAbaby Australia runs a Crash Exchange Program for exactly this: lodge the details within 30 days and the capsule or base is replaced. Do not sell or pass on a capsule that has been in an accident.

faq.q: Do I need adapters for the pram?

faq.q: What is the difference between a capsule and a convertible car seat?
faq.a: A capsule is a rearward-facing carrier that lifts out of the car and onto the pram, made for roughly the first year. A convertible seat stays in the car and grows with the child, rearward then forward facing, often to four years or beyond. Most Australian families use a capsule first, for the travel-system convenience in the newborn months, then move to a convertible seat. Not sure about a fitting?

faq.q: Will the Minu Duo fit through a standard doorway?
faq.a: Yes. The pram is 70.6 cm wide and it is designed to clear a 73 cm doorway, which is the standard internal width in most Australian homes.

faq.q: Can I use the Minu Duo from birth?
faq.a: Yes, both seats, as sold. That is unusual in a double this compact. Most side-by-sides need one child to be sitting up before you can use both seats.

faq.q: Is the Minu Duo suitable for twins?
faq.a: Yes. Both seats are the same size, both recline, and both are usable from birth, so neither twin is in the lesser seat.

faq.q: Will a Minu Duo fit in my boot?
faq.a: Folded it is 33 x 70.6 x 60.2 cm. It is wide rather than long, so the number to check against your boot opening is the 70.6 cm width.

faq.q: How heavy is the Minu Duo?
faq.a: 12.7 kg, which is around the weight of a single full-size pram for two seats.

faq.q: How much weight does each seat take?
faq.a: Up to 22.7 kg per seat, so it stays usable well into the toddler years for both children.

faq.q: How much can the basket hold?
faq.a: 11.3 kg across the one basket underneath.

faq.q: Are the Minu Duo seats reversible?
faq.a: No, both seats face forward. Side-by-side doubles are built this way so the frame stays narrow enough for a doorway.

The most defensible sustainability claim a pram brand can make is not about materials. It is about how long the product lasts, and whether it can be repaired and passed on. That claim we can already substantiate: Designed to be reconfigured One Vista frame carries a first child, a second and a third rather than being replaced Serviced for a decade Complimentary inspection and adjustment for up to ten years from purchase Repairable Wheels, canopies, harnesses, baskets and fabrics are stocked as spare parts Built to be handed on A serviced pram with available parts has a second and third life What follows is UPPAbaby's own published environmental programme, at Our Planet . Every claim below is one UPPAbaby makes and names a certification you can check, rather than a sentiment.

Flame retardants No added flame-retardant chemicals on any material in direct contact with a child, across the car seat range Chemical emissions GREENGUARD Gold certified: prams, the RumbleSeat, car seats and the at-home range. The standard tests the finished product for total VOC emissions, not the fabric on its own Leather Chrome-free, from LWG Gold certified tanneries, and REACH certified, which means the tanning process passes regular chemical compliance testing Suppliers Audited against ISO 9001 Named certifications rather than sentiment, on purpose. "GREENGUARD Gold" is a thing you can look up; "we care about the planet" is not, and under ACCC guidance the second is the riskier of the two to publish.

Cardboard FSC certified, so it comes from responsibly managed forests Inks Soy based on all printed materials and boxes, rather than petroleum based Design Developed to limit packaging and plastic waste, using recyclable materials Whether a particular carton is kerbside recyclable depends on your council, so check the label on the box rather than taking a general claim for it.

The honest answer is that the work here is about keeping a pram out of landfill for as long as possible, rather than recycling it at the end. Kept in service Free Tune-Up Days , a three year warranty, servicing for up to ten years, and spare parts sold individually Passed on Excess inventory is donated through UPPAbaby Gives Back, which has given more than US$3 million of gear to children in need There is no take-back or recycling scheme for a pram at the end of its life, and we would rather say so than imply one. A capsule retired under the Crash Exchange Program must not be resold or passed on at all.

UPPAbaby requires every supplier to maintain safe, slavery-free workplaces and audits them to check it, including workers' rights, contracts, working hours, overtime, leave, minimum wage and unions. Suppliers are audited against ISO 9001. This is UPPAbaby's own published position rather than a claim we make on their behalf. It is set out in UPPAbaby's Modern Slavery Statement , made under the United Kingdom's Modern Slavery Act.
Longevity is the environmental claim a pram brand can stand behind: one frame across three children, serviced for ten years, repaired with stocked parts.

Read the UPPAbaby warranty carefully and you will find this exclusion: damage resulting from airline shipping and handling is not covered. That is not unusual. No pram warranty covers a baggage handler. But it leaves a real hole, because gate-checking a pram is one of the most likely moments in its life for something to get bent. TravelSafe is the answer to that specific hole. Buy an UPPAbaby travel bag, register it, and air travel damage is covered under the terms of your original warranty. Why the bag is the condition The bag is not an upsell bolted onto the programme, it is the thing that makes the programme possible. A pram in a padded bag survives a hold; a pram gate-checked naked frequently does not. Requiring the bag is how the cover stays affordable.

faq.q: Can I use the Vista V3 from birth?
faq.a: Yes, straight out of the box. The bassinet is included, not an accessory you add later, so a newborn can lie flat on day one. The toddler seat takes over at around six months.

faq.q: How many children can a Vista V3 carry?
faq.a: Up to three on the one frame. Two seated, using a RumbleSeat or a second bassinet, and a third standing on a PiggyBack board that clips to the rear axle.

faq.q: Will a Vista V3 fit in my boot?
faq.a: Folded with the toddler seat attached it is 41.4 x 65.3 x 85.9 cm. With the seat removed it drops to 28.7 x 65.3 x 82.9 cm. Measure the shortest side of your boot opening, not the space inside it. The opening is what stops a pram going in.

faq.q: How heavy is the Vista V3?
faq.a: 12.5 kg with the frame and toddler seat together. The frame alone is 9 kg, the seat 3.5 kg and the bassinet 4.2 kg, so it can be lifted in parts.

faq.q: Does the Mesa capsule fit the Vista V3?
faq.a: Yes, directly. The Mesa clicks onto the frame with no adapters, so a sleeping baby goes from the car to the pram without being unbuckled. Maxi-Cosi, Nuna, Joie and BeSafe capsules fit with the Vista upper car seat adapter.

faq.q: What is included in the box?
faq.a: Pram frame, toddler seat, bassinet, bumper bar, seasonal seat liner, toddler seat bug shield, toddler seat rain shield, bassinet bug shield, storage bag and the three year warranty. Nothing on that list is sold separately.

faq.q: How much can the basket hold?
faq.a: 13.6 kg, which is the largest in the range. It is reachable from either side, including when the seat faces you.

faq.q: Does the seat face me or face out?
faq.a: Both. The toddler seat is reversible, so it can face you while they are small and face forward when they would rather watch the world.

This sounds trivial and it is the single biggest cause of delay. Daylight, near a window. Flash flattens exactly the detail we need. A short video if the fault is a movement or a noise. A squeak is easier to show than describe. The serial number label, readable.

faq.a: The warranty does not cover: Defects caused by misuse or poor maintenance. The instruction booklet sets out how the product should be used and looked after. Damage caused by improper installation of UPPAbaby parts or accessories. Corrosion, mould or rust caused by poor maintenance, servicing or storage. Normal wear and tear. Damage or degradation caused by sun, sweat, detergents, damp storage or frequent washing. Repairs or modifications carried out by a third party. Products bought from an unauthorised retailer. Second owners, and users other than the registrant. Damage caused by airline shipping and handling. Products that have been involved in an accident. UPPAbaby reserves the right to determine whether the warranty terms and conditions have been met. If your Mesa capsule has been in a car accident, the warranty is not the right programme. The warranty is not transferable . It extends only to the original retail purchaser and is valid only when supported by proof of purchase from an authorised retailer. Keep your receipt. The three years run from the date of purchase, so without a receipt showing that date there is no way to establish whether a product is inside its warranty period, and the claim cannot be assessed. This applies however the fault arose and however long you have owned the product. The warranty is valid only in the country of original purchase, and is subject to the conditions set by that country. Conditions vary between countries, and UPPAbaby will not ship replacement or repair parts outside the country of purchase. A pram bought overseas is not covered here. faq.q: Your rights under Australian Consumer Law
faq.a: This warranty sits on top of your rights under Australian Consumer Law. It does not replace them and cannot reduce them. Our goods come with guarantees that cannot be excluded under the Australian Consumer Law. You are entitled to a replacement or refund for a major failure, and to compensation for any other reasonably foreseeable loss or damage. You are also entitled to have the goods repaired or replaced if they fail to be of acceptable quality and the failure does not amount to a major failure. These guarantees apply for a reasonable period given the price and nature of the product, which for a pram at this price can be longer than three years.
